decompiler.options: the account's saved options, AI variable names off

sections.title: hand-written cases
sections.about: the 42 programs in cases/, each a shape that has tripped decompilers up

tests.name: builtins
tests.about: calls Luau turns into FASTCALL or folds when the arguments are constants: math, bit32, string and buffer, with arguments at their edges, and the same builtins through locals and upvalues

tests.name: calculator
tests.about: A tokenizer and recursive-descent parser for arithmetic, with variables and errors.

tests.name: captured_args
tests.about: a local that a closure assigns, read as an argument before a call that runs the closure

tests.name: closures
tests.about: upvalues, nested closures and recursion

tests.name: contextual_keywords
tests.about: `continue` is only a keyword where it can't be a variable: `while continue do` reads one

tests.name: control_flow
tests.about: branches and every loop kind

tests.name: dead_code
tests.about: a friend's case: a branch constant folding can prove dead (O1+ drops it entirely), with a numeric for over nils inside that would error if it ever ran

tests.name: debug_names
tests.about: compiled with debug level 2, so the real local names are in the bytecode

tests.name: deep_branches
tests.about: branch-heavy code (a friend's challenge): ifs nested 150 deep, 300 if/elseif/else in a row and 300 conditions with a dead `false and` part. A decompiler that retries a nested `if` on a failed attempt takes 2^depth steps here

tests.name: environments
tests.about: getfenv and setfenv: once a script touches environments, the compiler stops assuming globals are what they look like, so builtins aren't folded, fast calls check the environment and imports are looked up again. A decompiler has to keep every global a global

tests.name: evaluation_order
tests.about: evaluation order a decompiler can't move: locals used once whose calls have side effects, the operands of > and >= (compiled as < and <= with the operands swapped), a method call's object and arguments, and values read before a later write or call changes them

tests.name: events
tests.about: event handlers and loops over instance collections

tests.name: generalized_iteration
tests.about: generic for without an iterator function: plain tables (array part, then hash part), __iter returning a closure or next, objects with __call, coroutines, and pairs and ipairs, which the compiler turns into their own loop instructions

tests.name: if_local
tests.about: Luau's experimental `if local` / `while local` / `const` syntax (a friend's case). The binding lives only in the then-branch or loop body, so an outer variable with the same name has to stay visible in the else-branch, and every loop iteration gets a fresh local for closures.

tests.name: imports
tests.about: `a.b.c` on a global compiles to an import, looked up once when the script loads; with brackets it's read every time. The two have to stay apart

tests.name: inlining
tests.about: small local functions that -O2 copies into their callers

tests.name: inventory
tests.about: An inventory with stacking, weight limits and a sorted report.

tests.name: iterators
tests.about: for loops: generic for over custom iterators (stateless, stateful, next directly), numeric for with float and negative steps, bounds evaluated once, and a body that writes its loop variable

tests.name: literals
tests.about: literals that have to come back exactly: escapes, control bytes, long brackets that contain their own closers, numbers at the edges of what %.17g and hex can say, and -0

tests.name: loop_closures
tests.about: closures made in loops: each iteration of a for loop has its own variable, a while loop's local is fresh each time round, and an upvalue written after capture is shared

tests.name: loop_exits
tests.about: loops whose exits carry a value out, and a loop body that needs a goto to structure

tests.name: loops
tests.about: breaks, continues and returns out of loops, each checked by running both versions

tests.name: metatables
tests.about: metamethods: arithmetic, comparison, concat, call, index and newindex functions, len and unm, and the raw functions that skip them

tests.name: multiple_assignment
tests.about: multiple assignment and multiple returns: every right-hand side is read before anything is assigned, a call in the middle of a list is cut to one value, and parentheses cut it too

tests.name: nan_comparisons
tests.about: comparisons a decompiler can't flip: with NaN, `not (a < b)` isn't `a >= b`, and `x ~= x` is true. Also and/or chains where a false or nil value in the middle changes which side wins

tests.name: nested_inlining
tests.about: shapes from inlined helpers with control flow (-O2 copies them into their callers)

tests.name: numbers
tests.about: constants the compiler folds, and the places folding differs from running

tests.name: oop
tests.about: metatable classes with methods

tests.name: operators
tests.about: precedence and arithmetic corners a printer has to parenthesize or keep apart: unary minus against ^, not against ==, right-associative .. and ^, and Luau's floor division and modulo with negative and fractional operands

tests.name: pathfinding
tests.about: A* on a small grid map, with a binary heap for the open set.

tests.name: readability
tests.about: shapes the printer turns back into source sugar

tests.name: refusals
tests.about: shapes the new core used to refuse, mostly what -O2 inlining leaves behind

tests.name: register_pressure
tests.about: a function at Luau's limits: 190 locals (the cap is 200), a call with 60 arguments on top of them (registers stop at 255), a 100-entry constructor and closures over the first and last local. The compiler fits it; a decompiler that adds temporaries or declares more locals than the original had writes something that doesn't recompile

tests.name: roblox_names
tests.about: naming that leans on Roblox conventions, run against small stand-ins for the real APIs

tests.name: scopes
tests.about: locals that are written inside a loop and read after it, or in a repeat's condition

tests.name: services
tests.about: naming hints: services, children, modules, instances

tests.name: silent_effects
tests.about: work that never shows up in print: globals written and removed, a library table extended, tables changed through metamethods and table.insert/remove, coroutines resumed for their side effects, and what the chunk returns. Only what's left behind tells a right decompile from a wrong one, so the result has to be graded on that too

tests.name: strings
tests.about: interpolation and compound assignment edge cases

tests.name: table_constructors
tests.about: table constructors: positional entries overwrite earlier [1] =, a call or ... last expands but anywhere else gives one value, nil holes, and keys that need brackets

tests.name: tables_and_strings
tests.about: tables, varargs, multiple returns and string building

tests.name: type_syntax
tests.about: type syntax, which compiles to nothing, compiled with type information on (+t1): every function carries its parameter types in the bytecode, which a decompiler has to read past, and casts, generics, packs and attributes all have to come back as valid Luau

tests.name: vectors
tests.about: vectors: vector.create with constant arguments folds into a vector constant, which has to come back as something vanilla Luau runs (Roblox spells it Vector3.new, plain Luau doesn't have that), plus vector arithmetic, components and the vector library, which compile to fast calls

sections.title: libraries
sections.about: the 6 open-source libraries in libraries/, each graded by its own test suite: only the library is decompiled, then its spec runs against the output

tests.name: inspect
tests.about: inspect.lua 3.1.0 (kikito/inspect.lua a8ca312): human-readable dumps of nested tables, with cycle ids, sorted keys, escapes, depth limits and a process callback. Upstream's spec, run unchanged except where Luau differs from Lua 5.1 (see libraries/README.md)

tests.name: json
tests.about: json.lua 0.1.2 (rxi/json.lua dbf4b2d): a JSON encoder and decoder built on string scanning, character-class lookup tables and recursive descent. Upstream's test/test.lua with its own runner, unchanged except where Luau differs from Lua 5.1 (see libraries/README.md)

tests.name: libdeflate
tests.about: LibDeflate 1.0.2-release (SafeteeWoW/LibDeflate afc3b78): DEFLATE, zlib and preset-dictionary compression in 3,600 lines of pure Lua, with bit operations done in arithmetic and big functions full of locals and upvalues. Its upstream tests need io and luaunit, so this spec is Rosetta's own: every compressor setting round-trips a fixed set of inputs, and the compressed bytes are checksummed, so output that decompresses but differs still shows

tests.name: lume
tests.about: lume 2.3.0 (rxi/lume 98847e7): a grab bag of ~80 small functions over tables, strings, math and closures (memoize, combine, chain, lambda, serialize, wordwrap, color). Upstream's test/test.lua and its test/util/tester.lua, ported where Luau differs from Lua 5.1 (see libraries/README.md)

tests.name: middleclass
tests.about: middleclass 4.1.1 (kikito/middleclass 359f0e2): classes, subclasses, mixins and every metamethod Luau has, built from metatables and __index chains. Upstream's specs, run unchanged except where Luau differs from Lua 5.1 (see libraries/README.md)

tests.name: tween
tests.about: tween.lua 2.1.1 (kikito/tween.lua 9cdcd39): tweening with the full set of Penner easing functions, so mostly float arithmetic. Upstream's spec, unchanged except where Luau differs from Lua 5.1 (see libraries/README.md)
